steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Nucleosynthesis is the process by which stars create heavier elements from lighter ones through nuclear fusion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Main-sequence stars fuse hydrogen to helium via the proton-proton chain (lower mass) or CNO cycle (higher mass)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The triple-alpha process fuses three helium nuclei into carbon in red giant cores

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Massive stars can fuse elements up to iron (Fe) in successive shell layers — iron is the endpoint as fusion beyond iron absorbs energy

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why is iron the endpoint of stellar fusion? | Q: How are elements heavier than iron produced? | Q: What is the triple-alpha process?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Fusing iron or heavier elements absorbs energy rather than releasing it, so the star can no longer produce outward pressure to support itself. | They are produced during supernova explosions (r-process) and neutron star mergers, where extreme conditions allow rapid neutron capture to build heavier nuclei. | Three helium-4 nuclei (alpha particles) fuse to form carbon-12. This occurs in the cores of red giants after hydrogen fusion ends.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Iron is the fusion endpoint — this is key for both boards Elements > iron come from supernovae — this is a common exam answer Know the onion-shell model for massive stars: H → He → C → O → Ne → Si → Fe The triple-alpha process produces carbon — the basis of life
